text: The 2021 tree-cover loss of 81.3 ha (2.2% of the asset) was likely legal. The event occurred in a planted forest (68.1 ha of *Pinus elliottii* and *Pinus taeda*), not native forest (0 ha). Uruguay’s forest laws generally permit harvesting or clearing of planted forests if done in compliance with permits and sustainable practices. The loss was also fragmented, with 37.3 ha in patches under 0.5 ha (excluded from event classification). No evidence suggests the activity violated regulations, though further review of permits would confirm legality.
